title: Grateful Dead Live at Reno Centennial Coliseum on 1982-03-13
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Apogee Ensemble -> Peak -> AIFF  Mastering Info: AIFF -> Samplitude Professional v11.2 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Clean soundboard capture of a high‑energy second set featuring a smoking Stranger > Franklin’s, stellar Space into The Other One, and tight Eyes with a slipknot tease.
ai_review.review: The recording is a very clean soundboard source that lets the band’s chemistry shine. The second set bursts with highlights – a smoking Stranger > Franklin’s, an out‑of‑this‑world Space leading into a soaring Other One, and a tightly executed Eyes featuring a slipknot tease – all delivered with high energy. Reviewers note only minor quirks (a brief false start on He's Gone) and praise the overall performance.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently strong musical praise across most reviews, with excellent soundboard quality noted; only one low‑star comment, so the combined show and recording rating is high.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Very clean mix with distinct instrument separation; reviewers highlight crisp sound, great board balance, and no significant drop‑outs or muddiness.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Second set flows tightly with strong transitions; a brief three‑second confusion at the start of Eyes resolves quickly, keeping momentum high.

band_member_comments.Jerry: False start on He's Gone resolved into tight Eyes; notable slipknot tease at the end of Eyes; praised guitar exchange with Bob during Stranger.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass highlighted for ‘dropping bombs’ especially in the Spring/Summer ’82 vibe.
band_member_comments.Bob: Strong rhythm and vocal work, highlighted by a great Weir/Jerry exchange on Stranger.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent Mydland’s electric piano praised as fully integrated and adding depth to the set.
